questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is less damaging than listening to music.

questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Use hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: A motorcycle passenger should:

options.text: Put their feet on the operator's footrests.
Wear the same protective gear as the operator.
Make the operator sit closer to the handlebars than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear the same protective gear as the operator.
questions.explanation: A passenger should wear the same protective clothing and gear as the operator. The operator should not need to sit any farther forward when carrying a passenger.

questions.question: Which of the following is not protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe riders wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: To protect a motorcycle rider, pants should:

options.text: Be made of a soft material.
Be made of a heavy material.
Fit loosely enough that they flap in the wind.
Be short and expose some parts of the legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be made of a heavy material.
questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or heavy synthetic material that cover your entire legs. Pants should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but not so tight that they restrict movement.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces for motorcycles include wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers. Dry pavement provides good traction.

questions.question: What helps reduce the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?

options.text: Not allowing a passenger on the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most effective way to reduce head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: The body eliminates one alcoholic drink per hour. If a person drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks likely remain?
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours passed from the number of drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining.

questions.question: When approaching an object or uneven surface you cannot avoid, you should:

options.text: Make sure the motorcycle is leaning to one side.
Rise slightly off the seat to allow your legs to absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat to allow your legs to absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as possible and approach at a 90-degree angle. Keep the motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off your seat so your knees can absorb impact. Just before contact, roll on the throttle slightly to lighten the front end.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat that is large enough for two riders.
Only have one set of footrests.
Not encourage the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other motorists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat that is large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat for two riders and footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear as you.

questions.question: A DOT-compliant helmet has all of the following, except:

options.text: Bright colors painted on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors painted on the outside.
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner liner, a comfort liner, and a chinstrap retention system.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is a lot of traffic.

questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because motorcyclists and other drivers can collide there.

questions.question: For the best protection, wear a helmet certified by the:
questions.explanation: For the best protection, your helmet must meet U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, think about:

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead on the road.
Which position makes your trip shorter.
Which position lets you pass more vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should make sure other drivers can see you and that you have enough space around you.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time can lower your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot reduce alcohol in your body or make you sober, though they may keep you awake.

questions.question: What is often in the center of the lane?
questions.explanation: Oil drips from cars create a greasy strip in the center of each lane. In dry conditions, it is usually safe for a motorcycle to ride on this strip.

questions.question: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: In general, the body gets rid of almost ______ per hour.
questions.explanation: The average person's body can remove the alcohol in about one drink per hour.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If you can't avoid a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you can't avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go over it as slowly as possible.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should continually look ahead for:
questions.explanation: Look ahead to stay alert. Watch for changes in traffic, hazards on the road, and possible escape routes. Be ready to react quickly.

questions.question: The best way to handle someone tailgating you is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to get distance between you and them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass. If you speed up, they may speed up too, which makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, remember that motorcycles:

options.text: Are too small to have blind spots.
Have blind spots that are too small to cause problems.
Have blind spots that require you to turn your head to check.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that require you to turn your head to check.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When adjusting your rearview mirror, make sure you can see:

options.text: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
Only the lane next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the lane next to you as possible. The road behind and beside you is what matters most.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Assume everything on your motorcycle will work properly.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: A small mechanical problem on a motorcycle is more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.
